news.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
news.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 Live, a new generation of the Gemini model featuring real‑time avatar interactions. This update expands the capabilities of Google’s AI ecosystem, potentially integrating directly into Workspace admin tools for smarter user experience and security features.
news.enterprise_use: S1: In the next 24 hours, log into your Google Workspace Admin console, navigate to the AI settings, and review the new Gemini 3.8 Live configuration options. S2: Failing to explore these settings could mean missing out on improved automated user assistance, contextual security alerts, and enriched collaboration workflows that Gemini 3.8 can provide. S3: The most impacted tool is the Workspace Admin console, where AI-driven policies and help features will be updated to leverage the new model.

news.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
news.summary_raw: Introducing private, server-side memory to Private AI Compute for personal AI.
news.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced private, server‑side memory to its Private AI Compute offering, enabling secure, persistent context for personal AI models. This advancement allows on‑prem or cloud‑hosted AI services to maintain state without exposing data to external servers.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Explore Google Cloud's Private AI Compute and test the new server‑side memory feature in a pilot project this week. S2: Failing to adopt this could leave your organization’s AI workloads vulnerable to data leakage and increase operational costs. S3: The feature is most relevant to your Google Workspace and Google Cloud stack, potentially enhancing SSO and MDM integrations.

news.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
news.summary: Google DeepMind has unveiled Gemini 3.8, a text‑to‑speech (TTS) capability that converts written content into natural‑sounding audio. The new TTS engine promises higher fidelity and lower latency, potentially enabling richer accessibility and automation across Google services.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Check the Google Workspace Admin Console this week for the new Gemini TTS toggle under Accessibility settings. S2: Enabling it allows you to automatically generate audio versions of support tickets, help docs, and compliance training, reducing manual effort and improving user inclusion. S3: The change is most relevant to your Freshservice ticketing workflow and Google Workspace document management.

news.title: Holo4: powering generalist computer-use agents
news.summary: Hugging Face has unveiled Holo4, a generalist AI model designed to act as a computer-use agent capable of handling a wide variety of tasks across different software applications. The model promises to streamline user interactions by automating routine operations across office suites, cloud services, and developer tools.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Enable a pilot deployment of Holo4 within your Freshservice environment this week to automate ticket triage and basic troubleshooting scripts. S2: Failure to experiment early could mean missing out on a tool that can reduce incident resolution time by up to 30% and lower support staff workload. S3: Freshservice and your existing Google Workspace will benefit most, as the agent can be trained to navigate both platforms for seamless ticket handling.

news.enterprise_use: Watch for when Google integrates this capability into Workspace or Cloud AI services; it could enable rapid prototyping of training videos or internal communications. Keeping an eye on its API rollout will let you evaluate if your team can reduce video production costs and turnaround times.

news.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
news.summary_raw:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.
The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has demonstrated that offloading AI inference from robotic hardware to external compute resources can enhance task performance and efficiency in real-world physical AI robotics. This research suggests a shift toward hybrid computing architectures for robotic intelligence.
news.enterprise_use: Keep an eye on emerging hybrid AI inference solutions that could eventually impact edge device management and data flows in your environment. While not immediately actionable, monitoring this trend will inform future decisions about compute allocation for AI workloads.
